x: This man has run 32 minutes for 10k in the past and will be a great asset in times to come. Stage 6: Steve Clarke was well psyched up for his run and with runners strung out ahead set about them in no mean fashion.

Will Cockerell was first male Belgrave runner to reach the finish line in The Mall. Apart from clocking a useful time Will was running to collect money for RAPt (Rehabilitation for Addicted Prisoners Trust) a charity offering treatment to alcoholics and drug addicts in prison.

Phil Carstairs was in the 90s and Will Cockerell about 20 places further back. It needs six men to complete a team, however, and battling for that honour were Rob Harding, Darryl Ochse and Mike Kazimierski in the early 200s.

Soon he will be off to South Africa for six weeks so we must do without him in the road relays. Paul Freary was hoping for better than his 47th but what a superb and well-judged run from Alaster Stewart in 74th.
With the next team, Boxhill, now nearly two minutes behind, Will "Billy the Kid" Cockerell showed great confidence by moving up and forging a small lead.

First Belgravian home in the 2003 AAA Half Marathon at Wilmslow, first man home in the National Cross Country, winner of the Cross Country Plate for the second year in succession and now a AAA 12-Stage gold medallist. It seems the sky's the limit for Will.
Skipper Will went through 29 seconds faster than his relay split of 14:09 - and then proceeded to turn in another lap of 14:00 - while Tim Weeks was also inside his relay mark.
Will and Tom Ellacott were making up much ground now while up front Rodgers had got away from David, who then found himself being attacked by Herne Hill's Ian Lockett.

Most of the guys ahead of him will not be eligible for the World Cross Championships and with the confidence gained from this run, Kris has everything to go for when it comes to the trial at Nottingham in two weeks time.

When Andy didn't show up in the top 10, Will's heart rate went up a notch or two; when the top 15 were home and a Belgrave vest hove into sight – Karl's – the Skipper's pulse went into overdrive; and by the time he was away in 20th spot and 2 minutes 36 seconds down on the lead, his vital organs wer…

An appeal to the Race Referee met with a stone wall response. “You cannot run him - if you do then you will be disqualified.” While struggling to cope with this the TM then found that Richard Ward's name was also not on the declaration list.

Will's time of 13.85 for 4th, into a headwind, stood up as one of the fastest losers for a couple of races but by the time the last heat was run the wind had changed to become following at 2.0mps and Will's time was eclipsed by others.

Unfortunately Phil Wicks, winner though he was in the end, wonders whether he will run this one again. He suffered from a turned ankle on lap one, having broken clear of the field along with guesting Huw Lobb (Bedford &C).
